strengths.text: IT IS THE BEST-POSITIONED SIZE IN THE CATALOGUE FOR THE CLASS 3A ROUTE. 33.00 m2 is above the 32 m2 minimum and well below the 45 m2 maximum, so minor variation in the as-built figure will not push it out of the band — which cannot be said of the 45 m2 model. A ONE-BEDROOM LAYOUT IS ALSO THE COMMON REQUIREMENT for an elderly parent or a single adult, making this the range's mainstream product rather than an edge case. THE AREA IS PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED. NOT ESTABLISHED: no height, U-value, warranty, price, room dimensions or specification detail is published for this product.

IT EXTRACTS THE MAXIMUM PERMITTED SPACE FROM THE 2026 PROVISION. 45.00 m2 is 12 m2 more than the 1 Bed and, unlike the 48 m2 model, it remains inside the qualifying band — a well-judged product position. THE ONE-OR-TWO-BEDROOM FLEXIBILITY is a real advantage at this size: the same shell can house a couple or a parent with a visiting family, which materially widens who the building works for. THE AREA IS PUBLISHED IN THE PRODUCT NAME AND VERIFIED in the certified layers. NOT ESTABLISHED: no height, U-value, warranty, price or room dimensions are published, so the two layouts cannot be compared on evidence.

IT IS THE LARGEST HABITABLE UNIT IN THE RANGE AND THE ONLY UNAMBIGUOUS TWO-BEDROOM ONE. Where the 45 m2 model offers one or two bedrooms within a fixed shell, this is designed for two, which matters to a household housing a couple with a child or two adults who each need a room. ONCE FULL PLANNING IS ACCEPTED AS THE ROUTE, the Class 3A ceiling stops constraining the design at all — the 3 m2 overrun costs nothing further. THE AREA IS PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED. NOT ESTABLISHED: no height, U-value, warranty, price or room dimensions are published.

PURPOSE-BUILT FOR SAUNA USE, AS WITH THE REST OF THE RANGE — a cabin designed around heat, steam and ventilation rather than a general garden building adapted to it. That specialism is the one established advantage. NOTHING FURTHER IS ESTABLISHED, AND THAT INCLUDES ANY ADVANTAGE OVER THE QUU: no floor area, footprint, height, wall build-up, heater specification, warranty term, installation scope or price is held for the Aurea, and no distinction between the two Auroom models has been drawn from the model names or from brand positioning. WHAT HAS DELIBERATELY NOT BEEN DONE: with two undifferentiated records, it would be easy to present one as the premium option. Nothing supports that. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask Auroom directly what separates the Aurea from the Quu — size, heater, timber, glazing and price — because Atlas records no difference at all.

THE PRODUCT IS PURPOSE-BUILT FOR ITS FUNCTION, AND THAT IS WORTH SAYING PLAINLY. A dedicated outdoor sauna cabin is engineered around heat, steam and ventilation — timber selection, sealing and bench geometry all follow from that — in a way that a general-purpose garden room converted to sauna use is not. For a buyer whose requirement is a sauna, a specialist product is the right starting point. NOTHING ELSE IS ESTABLISHED IN ATLAS: no internal floor area, no external footprint, no height, no wall build-up, no heater specification, no warranty term, no installation scope and no price is held for the Quu, and nothing has been inferred from the wellness category or the brand. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the specialism is real; every number is still to be asked for.

NONE ESTABLISHED FROM PUBLISHED EVIDENCE. No construction specification, insulation data, glazing detail, warranty term, price or dimension is held for this record, so no strength can be stated and none has been inferred from the supplier's name or category. WHAT HAS DELIBERATELY NOT BEEN DONE: an Irish-sounding shed manufacturer invites an assumption of local supply, local installation and local aftercare, and that assumption has not been converted into a strength. Atlas records what the supplier publishes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat every claim you encounter about this product as unverified until you have it in writing from Ballyfree — starting with model names, external dimensions, wall build-up and what the price includes.

A DISTINCTIVE CURVED FORM WITH NO HABITABLE-USE BAGGAGE. For a homeowner who wants something other than a rectangular box and intends to use it as a studio, office or garden retreat, this is the model in the range that can at least reach the exemption question rather than failing before it. BERKO IS ISLAND-OF-IRELAND BASED, in Dungiven, Co. Derry, which shortens supply and support compared with the imported design-led records in this catalogue. NOT ESTABLISHED: no verified floor area, dimensions, height, insulation figure, warranty or price is published, so nothing about capacity or thermal performance has been recorded.

IT IS BUILT FOR THE USE IT NAMES. A lodge specified for overnight occupation is a different product from a garden office with a sofa in it, and for a buyer whose requirement is genuinely guest or holiday accommodation that honesty is useful — it points at the right regulatory route immediately rather than after a deposit. BERKO IS ALSO ISLAND-OF-IRELAND BASED, in Dungiven, Co. Derry, which is materially closer than the Baltic and UK-mainland manufacturers that dominate this catalogue's design-led records. NOT ESTABLISHED: Atlas holds no verified floor area, and no dimensions, height, insulation figure, warranty or price is published.

IT IS THE SMALLEST FORM IN THE RANGE AND THE MOST LIKELY TO SIT COMFORTABLY WITHIN A GARDEN, which matters when no floor area is published — a small building leaves more of the combined allowance intact whatever its exact footprint turns out to be. THE SHEPHERD'S HUT FORM ALSO SUITS A DAY-SPACE USE well: a single compact room with character, which is a genuine alternative to a rectangular garden office. BERKO IS ISLAND-OF-IRELAND BASED in Dungiven, Co. Derry. NOT ESTABLISHED: no verified floor area, dimensions, height, insulation figure, warranty or price is published, and its relative size within the range rests on the form's name rather than on any figure.

ONE STRENGTH IS ESTABLISHED AND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN TECHNICAL: because the size is specified per commission, the size decision and the planning decision become the same decision. On a plot that already holds a shed or a garage, that is worth more than any catalogue model's specification sheet — a fixed 24 m2 product either fits the remaining allowance or it does not, whereas a bespoke build can be drawn to fit it exactly. NOTHING ELSE IS ESTABLISHED. No construction system, wall build-up, insulation value, glazing specification, height, warranty term, installation scope or price is held in Atlas for this record, and no product URL exists. Nothing has been inferred from the word bespoke about build quality, which is a separate question entirely from flexibility.

FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE, THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST FOR THIS USE: the certified installation layer records that a client-facing space needs a CONSISTENT STANDARD OF FINISH, and that an ENGINEER-CERTIFIED FACTORY BUILD delivers that more reliably than an on-site assembly — where the finish depends on weather, access and the crew that turned up. No other supplier in this catalogue publishes an engineer sign-off before dispatch. TWO: the SIPS-PLUS-ECOTHERM PAIRING, recorded by the certified thermal layer as unmatched anywhere else in the Atlas — the insulation is the structure, so there is no repeating stud carrying heat around it, and the PIR core is the highest-performing common insulant per millimetre here. For a treatment room that is directly relevant: the certified record notes a client lying still for long periods needs a HIGHER AND STEADIER AIR TEMPERATURE than an office where someone is working and moving, and the envelope supports that. THREE: a published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE, the second-longest defined term in the Atlas. FOUR: A-rated low-E high-security glazing as standard, triple available, in PVC, aluminium or aluclad. FIVE: an Irish manufacturer with over twenty years' building experience, building complete and installing itself.

FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE, UNIQUE TO THIS CONFIGURATION: it is the only model in this supplier's Garden Room set that is genuinely SELF-CONTAINED — a bathroom and a kitchenette mean a long working day, a guest stay or a let does not require trips back to the house. That is what the planning question is about, and it is also the reason to want it. TWO: the SIPS-PLUS-ECOTHERM PAIRING recorded by the certified thermal layer as unmatched anywhere else in the catalogue — the insulation is the structure, so there is no repeating stud carrying heat around it, and the PIR core is the highest-performing common insulant per millimetre here. THREE: ENGINEER CERTIFICATION BEFORE DISPATCH, published by no other supplier in this catalogue. On a plumbed unit that matters more than on a shell, because concealed services are exactly what an on-site build hides. FOUR: a published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE, the second-longest defined term in the Atlas. FIVE: A-rated low-E high-security glazing as standard with triple glazing available, in PVC, aluminium or aluclad, from an Irish manufacturer with over twenty years' building experience. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: as a piece of building this is at the front of the catalogue; the reservations are all about consent.

FIVE STRENGTHS, and two of them are catalogue firsts. ONE, THE CONSTRUCTION PAIRING: the certified thermal layer records that Big Man combines the two strongest construction ideas found separately elsewhere in this Atlas — it builds in SIPS, so the insulation IS the structure and there is no repeating stud carrying heat around it, and it specifies ECOTHERM, a rigid PIR board, the highest-performing common insulant per millimetre in this catalogue. Loghouse also builds in SIPS but with a lower-performing EPS core. NO OTHER SUPPLIER MATCHES THAT PAIRING. TWO, THE ENGINEER CERTIFICATION: the unit is signed off by the supplier's own engineer BEFORE it leaves the factory. No other supplier in this catalogue publishes that step — the structure arrives as a certified object rather than as a building whose quality depends on what happened in a back garden on the day. THREE: a published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE, the second-longest defined term in the catalogue and by far the most striking in its Irish half, and materially more defensible written over a factory-built, engineer-certified product. FOUR: A-rated low-E glazing as standard with TRIPLE GLAZING AVAILABLE — only Garden Office Solutions fits triple as standard. FIVE: an Irish manufacturer with over twenty years' building experience, building complete units and installing them itself.

FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE: the SIPS-PLUS-PIR PAIRING. The certified thermal layer records that SIPS makes the insulation the structure, avoiding the stud cold-bridging that limits most framed garden rooms in this catalogue, and that EcoTherm is a rigid PIR board of the highest-performing common class — Loghouse builds in SIPS but with a lower-performing EPS core. No other supplier in the Atlas pairs the two. TWO: ENGINEER CERTIFICATION BEFORE DISPATCH, published by no other supplier in this catalogue — the quality risk moves off the site and into a controlled factory. THREE: a published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE, the second-longest defined term in the Atlas and the strongest in its Irish half. FOUR: A-rated low-E high-security glazing as standard, in PVC, aluminium or aluclad, with triple glazing available on request — a choice of frame material that very few suppliers here offer. FIVE, SPECIFIC TO THIS MODEL: an UNDIVIDED SPACE built to order. Where the storage and bathroom variants commit the footprint to a fixed layout, this one does not — useful precisely because the supplier custom-builds rather than shipping a standard model, so the internal arrangement can follow the intended use. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the best-constructed flexible shell in the catalogue.

WHAT CAN BE SAID APPLIES TO THE WHOLE MANUFACTURER RATHER THAN TO THIS MODEL: Lasita Maja publishes 'Wall dimensions' as EXTERNAL and 'Floor size' as INTERNAL, and the two reconcile to the centimetre on four separate products — a manufacturer whose figures can be trusted arithmetically, which is rare in this catalogue. IT ALSO OFFERS THE WIDEST WALL-THICKNESS LADDER IN THE ATLAS, from 19 mm to 92 mm, and the 92 mm option is the THICKEST SOLID TIMBER WALL RECORDED ANYWHERE in this catalogue. NOT ESTABLISHED FOR THIS PRODUCT: no dimensions, no area, no height, no wall thickness, no roof form, no price — and therefore no advantage claimed over any other Lasita model.

NINETEEN SQUARE METRES OF SUPPLIER-STATED INTERNAL FLOOR, CORROBORATED BY THE BASE DIMENSIONS — that combination is rare and it makes the product genuinely comparable on usable space rather than on a nominal label. A GABLE ROOF GIVES HEADROOM AND A MORE DOMESTIC APPEARANCE than the flat-roofed models in the range, and it opens the 4 m height allowance if a tiled or slated covering is chosen. DOUBLE GLAZING AND A FLOOR ARE INCLUDED, and a 70 mm log upgrade is offered at EUR 2,271. THE SUPPLIER IS IRISH VAT-REGISTERED with showrooms in Limerick and Wexford. NOT ESTABLISHED: no U-value, no insulation as standard, no roof covering as standard.

FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE, THE PLANNING OUTCOME IS DESIGNABLE. Every fixed-model supplier in this Atlas hands the buyer an area and leaves them to test it; here the area is an input. A room can be specified deliberately under the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, inside the 3 m flat-roof height limit, with the incidental-use condition designed for from the start. TWO, NO CRANE ACCESS REQUIRED — built on site from start to finish, so the delivery-access constraint that eliminates several well-specified competitors does not arise. THREE, 2–5 DAYS ON SITE, among the shortest build windows published in this Atlas. FOUR, A PUBLISHED STAGED PAYMENT SCHEDULE — 10 per cent to book, 50 per cent on day one, 40 per cent on completion, with finance on a soft credit check — which is rare in this catalogue and lets a buyer hold back the largest slice until the work is done. FIVE, A SHOWROOM at Mayobridge containing multiple finished rooms of different sizes, so the quality of finish can be judged directly. NEUTRALITY: these are process and design-freedom advantages. No thermal, structural or dimensional specification exists on which to rank this product against another, and Atlas has created none.

FIVE STRENGTHS, each traceable to a certified layer. ONE, YOU SET THE SIZE. This is a bespoke build — size, layout and external finish are chosen at design stage. For extra living space that matters more than it does for an office: the room has to fit the furniture and the family, not the other way round. TWO, ON-SITE CONSTRUCTION WITH NO CRANE. The certified installation layer records the building as constructed on site from start to finish, which removes the access constraint that rules out factory-built pods on tight or side-access-only plots. THREE, 2–5 DAYS ON SITE. Among the shortest build windows published anywhere in this Atlas, and materially less disruptive than the extension this product is positioned against. FOUR, A PUBLISHED STAGED PAYMENT SCHEDULE — 10 per cent to book, 50 per cent on day one, 40 per cent on completion, finance available on a soft credit check. Very few suppliers in this catalogue publish a schedule at all, and this one lets a buyer hold back 40 per cent until the work is done. FIVE, A REAL SHOWROOM at Mayobridge outside Newry containing 'multiple rooms all of different sizes and designs', so the finish can be inspected before ordering rather than judged from photographs.

FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT FOR A BESPOKE BUILDER ON THIS USE: YOU SPECIFY THE INTERNAL HEIGHT. Across this Atlas, gyms fail on clear height far more often than on floor area — Booths Garden Studios publishes a 2,080 mm standard it describes as low for overhead lifting, and Cabin Master publishes no height at all. Here the ceiling is a design decision rather than a fixed constraint, which is the single most useful thing a gym buyer can control. TWO, NO CRANE ACCESS REQUIRED. Built on site from start to finish, so a plot that cannot take a lift is not excluded. THREE, THE SUPPLIER ADDRESSES GYM USE EXPLICITLY rather than applying a gym label to a generic shell — equipment loading and noise reduction are both named in the published product description. FOUR, 2–5 DAYS ON SITE and a published staged payment schedule holding 40 per cent until completion. NEUTRALITY: the noise-reduction and equipment-handling claims are recorded as published and are not treated as an acoustic or structural specification; no specification exists to rank this product against another.

FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST CASE FOR THIS SUPPLIER OVER A POD MANUFACTURER: NO CRANE ACCESS IS REQUIRED. The building is constructed on site from start to finish, so the delivery-access question that eliminates several well-specified competitors before a quotation is even sought simply does not arise. TWO, THE PLANNING OUTCOME IS YOURS TO DESIGN. Because the footprint is set at design stage, an office can be specified deliberately under the 30 m2 combined allowance rather than accepted at whatever a fixed model happens to be — and a home office used by the occupants is the clearest case of incidental use there is, so this is the style in the range least likely to trouble the use condition. THREE, 2–5 DAYS ON SITE, among the shortest windows in this Atlas. FOUR, A PUBLISHED STAGED PAYMENT SCHEDULE with 40 per cent withheld until completion, plus finance on a soft credit check. FIVE, A SHOWROOM at Mayobridge outside Newry with multiple finished rooms, open Monday to Saturday by appointment — within reach of Republic buyers in the north-east.

FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE, THE BUILD WINDOW IS A COMMERCIAL ASSET: 2–5 days on site is among the shortest in this Atlas, and for a practitioner leaving rented rooms it means almost no lost trading. TWO, A PUBLISHED FINISH STANDARD — 'our garden rooms are completed to the highest standard of a builder's finish' — which matters more here than on any other style in the range, because a client judges the room the moment they walk in. THREE, THE LAYOUT IS YOURS. A treatment couch, a styling chair, a wash position and client circulation all have specific spatial requirements, and a bespoke builder can design around them where a fixed model cannot. FOUR, A SHOWROOM at Mayobridge with multiple finished rooms, so the finish a client will see can be inspected before ordering. FIVE, NO CRANE ACCESS REQUIRED, and a published staged payment schedule holding 40 per cent until completion — useful when the build is being funded from a business rather than a mortgage. NEUTRALITY: no specification exists on which to rank this product against another; the strengths above are process and design-freedom advantages, not measured performance.

FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE, AND IT IS GENUINELY UNUSUAL: THIS IS THE ONLY SENSORY ROOM PUBLISHED AS SUCH ANYWHERE IN THIS ATLAS. Across 385 certified Garden Room products and 59 suppliers, no other supplier names sensory use as a product. A family looking for this has, on published evidence, one supplier. TWO, THE DESIGN IS SPECIFIED BY THE BUYER. Sensory needs are individual — lighting, acoustics, floor area for equipment, door width for access, avoidance of particular finishes — and a bespoke builder can accommodate a specific requirement where a catalogue model cannot. THREE, THE BUILD IS SHORT AND ON SITE: 2–5 days, no crane, no module delivery. For a household where disruption is itself the difficulty, that is a substantive advantage over a multi-week build or a crane lift. FOUR, THE SUPPLIER NAMES COMFORT, INSULATION AND SOUND CONTROL as the design intent for this product specifically, rather than applying a generic shell to a sensory label. NEUTRALITY: those are stated intents, not measured specifications, and Atlas records them as published without treating them as performance figures.

NONE ESTABLISHED FROM PUBLISHED EVIDENCE. No construction system, wall build-up, insulation value, glazing specification, dimension, height, warranty term or price is held for this record, so no strength can be stated. WHAT HAS DELIBERATELY NOT BEEN DONE: the name invites an assumption about form — a cube implies a square plan and a flat roof, which would in turn imply a particular height condition and a particular usability. None of that has been inferred. A range name is not a specification, and across this catalogue model names have repeatedly proved to describe marketing positions rather than buildings. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat every claim you encounter about the CUBE range as unverified until the supplier gives you model-by-model figures in writing.

FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE, PLANNING EFFICIENCY: at 12 m2 this uses well under half the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, leaving roughly 18 m2 for a shed, a store or a future structure — the most accommodating of the three gyms on a plot that already has something standing. TWO: the envelope is identical to the largest product in the range — named silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm, double-glazed energy-efficient uPVC frames, EPDM or Kerbit SBS roofing, FSC MDF lining with a damp-resistant coating. That last item is the one that earns its place in a gym: exercise puts significant moisture into a small sealed room, and an uninsulated building would run with condensation on the walls. THREE: FOUNDATIONS INSIDE SCOPE alongside build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting. For a gym the floor takes dynamic load, and a single contract over base and building removes the dispute about which one failed. FOUR: two-to-four-day installation with no separate groundworks trade to schedule. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the same building quality as the 18 m2 model at two-thirds the garden footprint.

FOUR STRENGTHS, each traceable to a certified layer. ONE: the insulation is NAMED — Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm silver-backed rigid foam — where most of the catalogue uses the word 'insulated' without content. TWO: uPVC window and door frames, which conduct heat far less readily than the aluminium systems used elsewhere in the catalogue. THREE: FOUNDATIONS ARE INSIDE THE PRICE. Across this Atlas the base is the most commonly excluded item, and Cabin Master carries it alongside the build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting — so the quotation is closer to a delivered cost than most headline prices. For a gym this matters twice over: dropped weights and machine loads act on the floor structure, and one contractor is answerable for both base and building. FOUR: damp-resistant FSC MDF internal lining, directly relevant to the moisture load of training. FIFTH, ON PLANNING: at 15 m2 the unit sits half inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on envelope quality and contractual simplicity this is a strong position.

FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE: at 18 m2 this is the largest product in the Cabin Master range and the only one with enough floor for a rack plus cardio plus free floor space — the practical threshold for a gym that does not have to be rearranged between sessions. TWO: the specification does not change with size. The same named silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm, the same double-glazed uPVC, the same EPDM or Kerbit SBS roofing and the same damp-resistant FSC MDF lining as the smallest micro office. THREE: FOUNDATIONS INSIDE SCOPE, which carries more weight on this model than on any other in the range — dropped weights and machine loads act directly on the floor structure, and with base and building under one contract there is no argument about which of the two failed. FOUR: the two-to-four-day installation window is stated for this model as for the others, despite the increased size. FIFTH, ON PLANNING: 18 m2 remains within the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: full size, full specification, one contractor.

FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE: at 5 m2 this fits gardens that simply cannot accommodate a conventional garden room — a real capability, not a compromise, where the site is the binding constraint. TWO: the specification is NOT reduced to match the size. The supplier states its compact buildings 'share all the design features of our larger cabins', and the certified thermal layer records the same named silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm, the same double-glazed uPVC frames, the same EPDM or Kerbit SBS roofing and the same damp-resistant FSC MDF lining as the largest product in the range. Several suppliers in this catalogue thin the envelope on their smallest units; this one does not. THREE: ELECTRICS INCLUDED AND ITEMISED — double sockets, lighting and an ethernet point as standard, which at 5 m2 is unusual. FOUR: FOUNDATIONS INSIDE THE PRICE, along with the flooring and painting, over a two-to-four-day installation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the smallest footprint in the range without a corresponding drop in build quality.

FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE: a very small footprint that fits gardens where most garden rooms will not go, while still being the largest of the three micro offices — the one that carries a desk plus storage rather than a desk alone. TWO: ELECTRICS INCLUDED AND ITEMISED — double sockets, lighting and a dedicated ETHERNET POINT as standard. A wired network point at 7.36 m2 is rare in this catalogue and is the detail that marks the product as designed for working rather than storage. THREE: the insulation is named rather than merely asserted — Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm silver-backed rigid foam — with double-glazed uPVC frames, EPDM or Kerbit SBS roofing and a damp-resistant FSC MDF lining. FOUR: FOUNDATIONS INSIDE THE PRICE. GBP 15,550 carries the base, the build, the insulation, the electrics, the flooring and the painting, so it compares differently to a headline price that excludes groundworks — an exclusion priced elsewhere in this catalogue at EUR 3,000 to 4,000 plus VAT. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a like-for-like delivered basis this is a more complete number than it first appears.

Very small footprint at 3m x 2m, so it fits gardens where most garden rooms simply will not go. Electrics included as standard and itemised: double sockets, lighting and a dedicated ethernet point — wired connectivity is rare enough at this size to be a genuine differentiator for remote work.

FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE: the supplier names photography studios as a stated use case rather than leaving the buyer to adapt a generic office — the only product in the Cabin Master range positioned this way. TWO: the envelope is specified rather than asserted — named silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm; double-glazed energy-efficient uPVC frames; EPDM rubber or Kerbit SBS roofing; FSC MDF internal lining with a damp-resistant coating. Stable temperature matters for equipment as well as comfort. THREE: FOUNDATIONS, INTERNAL ELECTRICS, FLOORING AND PAINTING ARE ALL INSIDE THE SUPPLIER'S SCOPE, with a two-to-four-day site window and no separate groundworks trade to schedule. Studio use is power-hungry, so having the electrics installed under the same contract as the building is directly useful. FOUR, ON PLANNING: 15 m2 sits half inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, so area is not the constraint. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a well-specified shell delivered as one job; what it does not give you is the dimensional detail a studio actually turns on.

THREE FUNCTIONS IN ONE SMALL FOOTPRINT — room, storage and covered terrace — which on a compact plot is a more efficient use of the allowance than a plain box plus a separate shed. THE INDOOR AREA IS THE SUPPLIER'S OWN EXPLICIT INTERNAL STATEMENT, which makes the product rankable on usable floor where most competitors publish only a nominal size. 44 mm NORDIC SPRUCE MASSIVE LOGS with 18 mm floor and roof boards are published, and the supplier itemises its insulation option pricing openly — EUR 800 for floor and roof in 50 mm PIR, EUR 1,980 for 100 mm Rockwool, EUR 2,750 for walls. NOT ESTABLISHED: a reliable external footprint, no U-value, no roof covering as standard, no insulation as standard.

A BUILDING THAT SEPARATES CLEAN SPACE FROM DIRTY SPACE IS MORE USEFUL THAN ONE OPEN ROOM OF THE SAME AREA, and the second entrance means tools can be reached without walking through the main room. THE FIGURES RECONCILE EXACTLY — 360 × 456 cm less 28 mm each side is 15.96 m2, matching the published floor — so the area can be trusted. THE HEIGHT AND ROOF ANGLE ARE PUBLISHED, which settles the height condition without a phone call. NOT ESTABLISHED: no room-by-room split, no U-value, no confirmed Irish route, no warranty term for this model, and no evidence supporting workspace use — the manufacturer lists storage.

50-year structural warranty, the longest recorded on any Atlas Garden Room. 100mm galvanised box steel frame with 100mm insulated floor, walls and roof — no timber to rot or re-treat. Aluminium plate cladding, aluminium Low-E tempered double glazing and SPC flooring standard. Wired shell included. Compact 17m² footprint fits sites that cannot take the larger cabins in the range.

19.1m² at EUR 31,000, roughly EUR 1,623 per m² — better value than the 17m² and 25m² cabins in the same range. 50-year structural warranty, the longest in Atlas. 100mm galvanised box steel frame with 100mm insulated floor, walls and roof; aluminium plate cladding, aluminium Low-E tempered double glazing, SPC flooring. Wired with smart-home technology. Factory-finished and delivered, not site-assembled.

50-year structural warranty, the longest in Atlas. 100mm galvanised box steel frame with 100mm insulated floor, walls and roof — a maintenance-free envelope with no timber to treat. Aluminium plate cladding, aluminium Low-E tempered double glazing and SPC flooring standard. Wired and plumbed, ready for connection, which is a step beyond the wired-shell specification on the smaller cabins in the range. 25m² delivered factory-finished.

Best cost per square metre in the Concept Modular range at roughly EUR 1,481/m², and EUR 11,250 less than the 25m² cabin despite being a square metre larger. 50-year structural warranty, the longest in Atlas. 100mm galvanised box steel frame with 100mm insulated floor, walls and roof; aluminium plate cladding, aluminium Low-E tempered double glazing, SPC flooring. Wired with smart-home technology. 26m² is enough for a studio with a distinct working and living zone.

50-year structural warranty, the longest in Atlas. 100mm galvanised box steel frame with 100mm insulated floor, walls and roof; aluminium plate cladding, aluminium Low-E tempered double glazing and SPC flooring standard. Wired with smart-ready fittings. Top of the Concept Modular cabin specification at this size, delivered factory-finished with no site build to manage.

36.2m² delivered with a designer kitchen and bathroom fitted and a water heater as standard — genuinely habitable on arrival rather than a shell. 50-year structural warranty, the longest in Atlas. 100mm galvanised box steel frame with 100mm insulation throughout; aluminium plate cladding, aluminium Low-E tempered double glazing, SPC flooring. 3m external height with a terrace. Roughly EUR 1,877 per m² — better value than the Signature Cabin 25m² despite far higher specification.

50-year structural warranty, the longest recorded on any Atlas Garden Room. 100mm galvanised box steel frame with 100mm insulation throughout floor, walls and roof — no timber element to rot or require annual treatment. Aluminium plate cladding, aluminium Low-E tempered double glazing and SPC flooring standard. Wired with smart-ready fittings. Irish-supplied and factory-finished rather than site-built.

50-year structural warranty — by a wide margin the longest in Atlas, against 10 years from Luxury Garden Studios and a conditional 10-year anti-rot cover from Waltons. 100mm galvanised box steel frame with 100mm insulation to floor, walls and roof, so no timber to rot or re-treat. SOLID CEDAR CLADDING ON A FRAMED BUILD. THE TURNKEY SCOPE covers design, foundations, build, insulation, electrics and interior finish.
